clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old female with first consanguineous parents presented with a 10-year history of recurrent left-sided migrainous headaches and intermittent ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy (ptosis and horizontal diplopia) since age 8. Episodes occurred at ages 8, 13, 16, and 17, resolving spontaneously after approximately one month without treatment. Between episodes, she developed increasingly frequent disabling headaches. Brain MRI performed one year after the last attack revealed an enhancing nodule on the cisternal segment of the left oculomotor nerve (E001). The persistent nodular enhancement during asymptomatic periods was considered highly suggestive of schwannoma (E003). On follow-up, she experienced no additional episodes of ophthalmoplegia (E002). The diagnosis was established on clinical-radiological grounds without histopathological confirmation.
